title: Transport of a horizontal square-pasting equation through coherent comparisons
statement:
Let $A,B,C,D,E,F$ and their primed counterparts be categories with six functors $E_X:X\to X'$. Let $K:A\to B$, $L:B\to E$, $I:C\to D$, $J:D\to F$, $R:C\to A$, $P:D\to B$, $Q:F\to E$, $K_{12}:A\to E$, $I_{12}:C\to F$, with primed counterparts. Use the natural-transformation square notation of [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate], without requiring adjunctions. For functors $E_X:X\to X'$ and $F:X\to Y$ equipped with an invertible natural comparison $e_F:E_YF\simeq F'E_X$, put $e_{HF}=(H'e_F)\circ(e_HF)$ for a composite $HF$. For a cell $t:F\to H$ with the same endpoints, say it is respected if $e_H\circ E_Y(t)=(t'E_X)\circ e_F$. All compositions below are in the usual right-to-left order, with the canonical functor associators inserted. Choose the nine corresponding invertible comparisons. Let $c_K:LK\simeq K_{12}$ and $c_I:JI\simeq I_{12}$, and primed counterparts, satisfy $e_{K_{12}}\circ E_E(c_K)=(c'_KE_A)\circ e_{LK}$ and $e_{I_{12}}\circ E_F(c_I)=(c'_IE_C)\circ e_{JI}$. Let $a:PI\to KR$, $b:QJ\to LP$, $c:QI_{12}\to K_{12}R$ and primed counterparts be respected cells. If
$$ c'\circ(Q'c'_I)=(c'_KR')\circ(L'a')\circ(b'I'),$$
then for every $N\in C$,
$$ E_E\big((c\circ Qc_I)_N\big)=E_E\big(((c_KR)\circ(La)\circ(bI))_N\big).$$
The functors $E_X$ need not be faithful.

proof.text:
Fix $N\in C$ and put $n'=E_C(N)$. Write $e_T(M)$ for the forward component of a comparison, and write $E_X(u)$ for its action on a morphism. Set
$$s=e_{QJI}(N),\quad u=e_{QI_{12}}(N),\quad v=e_{LKR}(N),\quad w=e_{LPI}(N),\quad t=e_{K_{12}R}(N).$$
For example, repeated use of the given composite convention gives
$$\begin{aligned}
s&=Q'J'(e_I(N))\circ Q'(e_J(IN))\circ e_Q(JIN),\\
u&=Q'(e_{I_{12}}(N))\circ e_Q(I_{12}N),\\
v&=L'K'(e_R(N))\circ L'(e_K(RN))\circ e_L(KRN),\\
w&=L'P'(e_I(N))\circ L'(e_P(IN))\circ e_L(PIN),\\
t&=K'_{12}(e_R(N))\circ e_{K_{12}}(RN).
\end{aligned}$$
Both parenthesizations of a triple composite give exactly these products, by functoriality and associativity. The canonical functor associators have identity components, so they do not alter these component formulas. In particular, $s:E_E(QJIN)\to Q'J'I'(n')$ and $t:E_E(K_{12}RN)\to K'_{12}R'(n')$.

proof.text:
Naturality of $e_Q$ at $(c_I)_N: JIN\to I_{12}N$, followed by the assumed compatibility of $c_I$, gives
$$\begin{aligned}
u\circ E_E\bigl(Q((c_I)_N)\bigr)
&=Q'(e_{I_{12}}(N))\circ Q'\bigl(E_F((c_I)_N)\bigr)\circ e_Q(JIN)\\
&=Q'\bigl((c'_I)_{n'}\bigr)\circ s.
\end{aligned}$$
Here the second line substitutes $e_{I_{12}}(N)\circ E_F((c_I)_N)=(c'_I)_{n'}\circ J'(e_I(N))\circ e_J(IN)$ and uses that $Q'$ preserves composition. The respected-cell hypothesis for $c$ is $t\circ E_E(c_N)=c'_{n'}\circ u$. Composing these equalities, and using that $E_E$ preserves composition, yields
$$t\circ E_E\bigl(c_N\circ Q((c_I)_N)\bigr)=c'_{n'}\circ Q'\bigl((c'_I)_{n'}\bigr)\circ s.$$

source.place: Tag 0F7D, lemma-shriek-proper-and-open-compose-horizontal; agent component comparison calculation for its horizontal pasting equation

proof.text:
Evaluate the compatibility of $c_K$ at $RN$. Postcompose it with $K'_{12}(e_R(N))$ and use naturality of $c'_K:L'K'\to K'_{12}$ at $e_R(N):E_A(RN)\to R'(n')$. This gives
$$\begin{aligned}
t\circ E_E((c_K)_{RN})
&=K'_{12}(e_R(N))\circ(c'_K)_{E_A(RN)}\circ e_{LK}(RN)\\
&=(c'_K)_{R'(n')}\circ L'K'(e_R(N))\circ e_{LK}(RN)\\
&=(c'_K)_{R'(n')}\circ v.
\end{aligned}$$
The last line is just the expansion of $e_{LK}$ and the definition of $v$ in Step 1.

source.place: Tag 0F7D, lemma-shriek-proper-and-open-compose-horizontal; agent component comparison calculation for its horizontal pasting equation

proof.text:
Naturality of $e_L$ at $a_N:PIN\to KRN$ gives $e_L(KRN)\circ E_E(L(a_N))=L'(E_B(a_N))\circ e_L(PIN)$. Also the respected-cell equation for $a$ expands to
$$K'(e_R(N))\circ e_K(RN)\circ E_B(a_N)=a'_{n'}\circ P'(e_I(N))\circ e_P(IN).$$
Substitute these two equations into the expansion of $v$, and use that $L'$ preserves composition:
$$\begin{aligned}
v\circ E_E(L(a_N))
&=L'\bigl(K'(e_R(N))\circ e_K(RN)\circ E_B(a_N)\bigr)\circ e_L(PIN)\\
&=L'(a'_{n'})\circ L'P'(e_I(N))\circ L'(e_P(IN))\circ e_L(PIN)\\
&=L'(a'_{n'})\circ w.
\end{aligned}$$

source.place: Tag 0F7D, lemma-shriek-proper-and-open-compose-horizontal; agent component comparison calculation for its horizontal pasting equation

proof.text:
The respected-cell equation for $b$, evaluated at $IN$, is $e_{LP}(IN)\circ E_E(b_{IN})=b'_{E_D(IN)}\circ e_{QJ}(IN)$. Naturality of $b':Q'J'\to L'P'$ at $e_I(N):E_D(IN)\to I'(n')$ therefore gives
$$\begin{aligned}
w\circ E_E(b_{IN})
&=L'P'(e_I(N))\circ b'_{E_D(IN)}\circ e_{QJ}(IN)\\
&=b'_{I'(n')}\circ Q'J'(e_I(N))\circ e_{QJ}(IN)\\
&=b'_{I'(n')}\circ s.
\end{aligned}$$
The first and last lines expand the composite comparisons according to Step 1.

source.place: Tag 0F7D, lemma-shriek-proper-and-open-compose-horizontal; agent component comparison calculation for its horizontal pasting equation

proof.text:
Combining Steps 3, 4 and 5, with functoriality of $E_E$, gives
$$\begin{aligned}
t\circ E_E\bigl((c_K)_{RN}\circ L(a_N)\circ b_{IN}\bigr)
=(c'_K)_{R'(n')}\circ L'(a'_{n'})\circ b'_{I'(n')}\circ s.
\end{aligned}$$
The assumed primed horizontal-pasting equation evaluated at $n'$ identifies the right side with $c'_{n'}\circ Q'((c'_I)_{n'})\circ s$, which is the right side of Step 2. Thus the two morphisms asserted equal in the conclusion become equal after postcomposition with $t$. This $t$ is invertible: an explicit inverse is $e_{K_{12}}(RN)^{-1}\circ K'_{12}(e_R(N)^{-1})$, using preservation of composition and identities by $K'_{12}$. Postcompose the equality with this inverse and cancel $t^{-1}\circ t=1$. This is the claimed equality for arbitrary $N$; no equality is reflected through $E_E$.

Step 1: the component formulas for s, u, v, w, t, with both parenthesizations agreeing. Step 2: naturality of e_Q at (c_I)_N, then the c_I compatibility, then the respected-cell equation for c. Step 3: the c_K compatibility at RN, then naturality of c'_K at e_R(N), giving v. Step 4: naturality of e_L at a_N, then L' applied to the respected-cell equation for a. Step 5: the respected-cell equation for b at IN, then naturality of b' at e_I(N). Step 6: the primed pasting hypothesis at n', then cancelling the invertible t.
